question: What does the Chinese idiom '{{zh-CN|画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú|hwah shuh tyen dzoo}}' (literally: "draw a snake and add feet") mean?
correctAnswer: Ruin something by adding unnecessary extras.
incorrectAnswers: Finish a job with great skill.
explanation: This idiom is used in everyday chinese for the idea 'Ruin something by adding unnecessary extras.'. Word-to-word: "draw a snake and add feet." In the old story, a man who drew feet on his snake lost the contest, because snakes have no feet. Example: "这个设计已经很好了，再加装饰就是画蛇添足。" (The design was already good; adding decoration would only spoil it.)

question: What does the Chinese idiom '{{zh-CN|炒冷饭|chǎo lěng fàn|chow lung fahn}}' (literally: "to stir-fry cold rice") mean?
correctAnswer: Rehash old material with nothing new.
explanation: This idiom is used in everyday chinese for the idea 'Rehash old material with nothing new.'. Word-to-word: "to stir-fry cold rice." Fried leftover rice is the same old food served again. Example: "这部电影只是炒冷饭，没有新意。" (This film just rehashes old stuff and has nothing new.)
